name: Stardog
tagline: Enterprise knowledge-graph platform: RDF store, reasoning and virtual graphs over your sources.
description: Stardog is a commercial knowledge-graph platform built around an RDF/SPARQL engine with OWL and rule-based reasoning, edge properties (RDF-star) and virtual graphs that query relational, NoSQL and CSV sources in place instead of copying them. It also exposes GraphQL and a SQL endpoint for BI tools, and its Voicebox layer adds LLM-driven natural-language querying. Stardog targets enterprise data integration, where a semantic layer over many silos is worth the license; it is less attractive for simple app graphs or teams that want open source.

pricing.notes: Stardog Free is a renewable one-year license without HA, backups or full connectors; Enterprise and Cloud are quoted.

scale.notes: HA cluster replicates the full dataset; virtual graphs push queries to sources so not all data must be loaded.

strengths: Virtual graphs query relational and NoSQL sources in place, reducing ETL
Query-time OWL and rule reasoning without materializing inferred triples
Edge properties (RDF-star) bridge RDF and property-graph modeling
SQL endpoint lets BI tools read the knowledge graph directly
weaknesses: Proprietary with quote-based pricing; the free tier lacks HA and backups
Cluster mode replicates rather than shards, so dataset size is bounded per node
Reasoning-heavy queries can be hard to predict and tune
Smaller developer community than mainstream graph databases
useCases: Enterprise data fabric and semantic layer
Natural-language question answering over enterprise data
